question: Will the ZNPP's 750 kV Dniprovska line be reconnected/available as of October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is firmly NO and the resolution rule defaults to NO: IAEA Update 366 (11 Sep 2026) says Dniprovska 'remains unavailable despite repairs completed in June ... because of severe damage at the associated electrical substation', and Update 367 (17 Sep) calls Ferosplavna-1 the 'sole remaining external power line'. The line itself was repaired 21 Jun 2026; the gating item is a substation >100 km NW on Ukrainian-controlled territory damaged in late May, which WNN reported in June was 'not expected to be completed in the near term' and for which no completion date has ever been announced. Rosatom (~12 Sep) says the Russian-side work is done and energization depends on the Kyiv-controlled side; ZNPP's spokesperson (20 Sep) states only an undated intent to connect. Base rate: the line has sat unavailable through ~18 consecutive 10-day windows since 24 Mar 2026, with the substation blocker specifically unresolved for ~3 months. Upside paths — a quiet substation completion (needs no ceasefire, so it could arrive unsignalled), winter/diesel-reserve pressure, and the fine print counting even momentary energization — are real but do not fit a 9-day window absent any current signal. Reporting lag is a minor extra drag: restoration must also appear in an update published on/before 1 Oct (next due ~24 Sep and ~1 Oct) or in credible reporting.

calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the most recent IAEA Director General Update on the Situation in Ukraine published on or before 1 Oct 2026 (ReliefWeb/IAEA), NOT off plant-operator or Rosatom statements, and NOT off the 330 kV Ferosplavna-1 line or diesel generators. Fine print: if no IAEA update appears between 12 Sep and 1 Oct 2026 and no credible source reports a change, it resolves on last known status (unavailable). Even momentary/partial energization reported by IAEA as restoring the line to service counts as connected.

EVENT WINDOW: 2026-09-12 -> 2026-10-01 per the criteria; as of Now (2026-09-21T13:26Z) ~50% elapsed (9.6 of 19.0 days).

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: the line is described as unavailable.

EVIDENCE:
- IAEA Update 366, 11 Sep 2026: 'The ZNPP's other external power line - the 750 kV Dniprovska line - remains unavailable despite repairs completed in June under a previous IAEA-brokered ceasefire because of severe damage at the associated electrical substation.' No restoration timeline given.
- IAEA Update 367, 17 Sep 2026 (most recent published as of Now): does not name Dniprovska; describes Ferosplavna-1 as 'the ZNPP's sole remaining external power line ... which remains functional today', reconnected 7 Sep after the 7th IAEA-brokered localized ceasefire (demining/work 5-7 Sep).
- Dniprovska disconnected 24 Mar 2026 (military activity). Line repairs completed 21 Jun 2026 under the 6th IAEA-brokered ceasefire, across high pylons over the Dnipro.
- Blocker: an associated substation >100 km NW of ZNPP, on Ukrainian-controlled territory, damaged by military activity in late May 2026; IAEA experts who visited observed 'severe damage to essential equipment' (World Nuclear News, late Jun 2026).
- World Nuclear News, Jun 2026: substation repair efforts 'not expected to be completed in the near term, but are on-going.' No public completion date has been announced at any point since.
- Rosatom head Likhachev, ~12 Sep 2026 (Russian media): repair work on the Dniprovska line is complete and infrastructure fully restored 'from the Russian side'; supply cannot resume without the line being energized from Kyiv-controlled territory.
- ZNPP communications director Yevgenia Yashina, 20 Sep 2026 (Ridus, via AskNews): plant aims to connect the repaired Dniprovska line to cut dependence on diesel fuel and the single remaining line; as of that date it remains unconnected; no date or condition stated. ZNPP also said in Jun 2026 it was 'ready for voltage supply' via Dniprovska (RIA, 23 Jun) — readiness claims have recurred without energization following.
- Off-site power fragility: ZNPP has lost off-site power 26 times since 2022, including 10 times since Jun 2026 (Al Jazeera / IAEA). The 20 Aug - 7 Sep outage lasted ~19 days, the second-longest on record; a prior outage ran ~1 month (23 Sep - 23 Oct, earlier year).
- Grossi, Sep 2026: restoration of off-site power 'eased an immediate risk of station blackout, but further action is needed to stabilize the plant's increasingly fragile power situation and replenish its depleted diesel fuel reserves' — i.e. active IAEA pressure toward a second line, with winter approaching.
- Satellite imagery reported (Sep 2026, intent.press) showing construction of a new power line linking ZNPP toward Crimea — an alternative Russian-side grid path independent of Dniprovska.
- Contextual friction: energizing the 750 kV line requires action by the Ukrainian side; the same line is the export-capable path associated with any future reactor restart.

BASE RATES:
- Over the Dniprovska outage itself: unavailable continuously from 24 Mar 2026 to Now, i.e. ~18 consecutive 10-day windows with no restoration.
- Over the sub-period conditioned on the current blocker (substation damage, reported from late Jun 2026): ~9 consecutive 10-day windows with no restoration and no announced completion date.
- Over ZNPP line restorations generally: restorations of severed external lines in this conflict HAVE occurred repeatedly (Dniprovska restored after earlier multi-week/month outages; Ferosplavna-1 restored 7 Sep 2026) — typically via an IAEA-brokered localized ceasefire with publicly visible lead-up (negotiation, demining, field-team observation) spanning weeks. Seven such ceasefires to date.
- Asymmetry worth carrying: the current blocker sits in Ukrainian-held territory >100 km from the front, so its repair needs no ceasefire and could complete without the public signalling that preceded past restorations.

IAEA PUBLICATION CADENCE: numbered updates roughly weekly; 366 on 11 Sep (Fri), 367 on 17 Sep (Thu). On that cadence one update falls ~24 Sep and one ~1 Oct, both inside the window. No Update 368 found as of Now.

MARKETS: harness title-search found no Polymarket or Manifold candidate; my own check found no Kalshi contract and no bookmaker pricing this event. No crowd anchor exists.

SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND: any announced or estimated completion date for the damaged substation; any Ukrenergo/Energoatom statement on substation repair progress since June; any report of an 8th IAEA-brokered arrangement or scheduled energization test for Dniprovska; IAEA Update 368; any news dated 18-21 Sep 2026 on Dniprovska beyond the 20 Sep ZNPP-spokesperson remarks. The OECD-NEA status tracker is stale (last entry 16 Apr 2026).
calls.reference_class: ZNPP external power lines reported unavailable by the IAEA, hazard of restoration within a given ~10-day window, conditioned on (a) no announced repair-completion date and (b) the blocking repair sitting on the opposing side's territory

calls.reasoning: Line down since 24 Mar 2026 (~26 weeks). Line repairs finished June 2026, but the binding constraint is destroyed equipment at the Dniprovska substation 100+ km NW on Ukrainian-controlled territory, described by the IAEA in late June as under repair and not expected to finish in the near term. IAEA Update 367 (17 Sep 2026) still describes Ferosplavna-1 as the plant's 'sole remaining external power line'; a 20 Sep 2026 ZNPP-side statement confirms the repaired Dniprovska line is still not connected. Base rate of a status flip in any given ~10-day window since March: 0 of ~18, and the causal path (substation rebuild + energization from the Ukrainian side + IAEA reporting it by 1 Oct) has no observed progress. Residual YES mass comes from an unannounced substation completion, a sudden IAEA-brokered arrangement (seven have occurred), or a momentary energization counting as YES; fine print makes silence resolve NO, and reporting lag near the deadline further trims YES.

EVENT WINDOW: 12 Sep 2026 -> 1 Oct 2026 per the criteria's fine print; as of 2026-09-21T13:26Z, ~50% elapsed (9.6 of 19 days).
EVIDENCE:
- 24 Mar 2026: Dniprovska line disconnected due to military activity (background; IAEA updates).
- Late May 2026: the Dniprovska substation, 100+ km NW of ZNPP on Ukrainian-controlled territory, damaged by military activity; IAEA experts who visited observed severe damage to essential equipment (IAEA Update 355 / World Nuclear News, 26 Jun 2026).
- 21/26 Jun 2026: repairs to the LINE itself completed under the sixth IAEA-brokered localized ceasefire; line could not be returned to service; IAEA said substation repair efforts were ongoing but not expected to be completed in the near term (WNN 26 Jun 2026; Ukrainska Pravda 26 Jun 2026).
- 20 Aug 2026: ZNPP lost Ferosplavna-1, its then-only line; 26th total loss of off-site power; ~18-19 days on emergency diesel generators (IAEA Update 366; Al Jazeera 29 Aug 2026).
- 5-7 Sep 2026: seventh IAEA-brokered localized ceasefire enabled demining and repair; Ferosplavna-1 reconnected evening of 7 Sep at 19:02, plant consuming ~11 MW (IAEA Update 366, 11 Sep 2026; Energoatom via UNN).
- 11 Sep 2026 (IAEA Update 366): Dniprovska 'remains unavailable despite repairs completed in June ... because of severe damage at the associated electrical substation.'
- 12 Sep 2026: Rosatom head Likhachev said Rosatom repeatedly notified the IAEA that repair work on the Dniprovska line is complete; infrastructure fully restored on the Russian-controlled side; energization requires power fed from Kyiv-controlled territory (Russian media, profile.ru/osnmedia).
- 17 Sep 2026 (IAEA Update 367): refers to Ferosplavna-1 as the ZNPP's 'sole remaining external power line ... which remains functional today'; no reported change to Dniprovska.
- 20 Sep 2026: ZNPP communications director Yashina said the plant wants to connect the repaired Dniprovska line to cut diesel dependence; states it was repaired 21 Jun 2026 and is still not connected to the system (Ridus).
- Counter-direction factors on record: seven localized ceasefires have been brokered since 2025, showing both sides will agree to narrow nuclear-safety work; the plant's diesel reserves are depleted, giving urgency; IAEA teams are on site and at the substation; both Russian operators and the IAEA publicly want the second line restored; a momentary/partial energization reported by the IAEA as restoring service would count.
- Counter-direction factors the other way: the blocking asset is on Ukrainian-controlled territory and its energization is contested because a restored 750 kV connection is a prerequisite for any Russian restart of the reactors; three months elapsed (late Jun -> late Sep) with no public report of substation repair progress.
BASE RATES: over the ~26 weeks since 24 Mar 2026, zero IAEA updates have described Dniprovska as available (0 of ~18 ten-day windows). Conditioned on 'line itself repaired but substation destroyed' (since late Jun 2026), 0 of ~9 ten-day windows. Over the whole war (2022-2025), by contrast, Dniprovska outages were typically resolved within days to a few weeks whenever the blocking damage was to the line/switchyard rather than to a distant substation. IAEA update cadence 2026: roughly weekly (365, 366 = 11 Sep, 367 = 17 Sep), so ~1-2 further updates are expected before 1 Oct.
SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND: any report of Dniprovska substation repairs being completed or scheduled; any eighth localized ceasefire covering substation/energization work; any IAEA Update 368; any prediction market on this question at Polymarket, Kalshi, or Manifold; any stated target date from Ukrenergo, Energoatom, Rosatom, or the IAEA for returning the line to service.

calls.reasoning: Status quo is NO and the fine print makes NO the default if nothing is published. The Dniprovska line has been unavailable since 24 Mar 2026 (181 days) and unconnected despite completed line repairs since 21 Jun 2026 (92 days), with the binding constraint being severe damage to a 750 kV substation ~100 km NW of the plant — long-lead high-voltage equipment, reported in June as 'not expected to finish soon' and not mentioned as progressing in Updates 366 (11 Sep) or 367 (17 Sep). IAEA 367 explicitly still calls Ferosplavna-1 the 'sole remaining external power line,' and Russian plant management on 20 Sep still described the line as repaired-but-unconnected, so no update before the deadline has flipped it. Only ~9-10 days remain, and reconnection would additionally have to be captured in an IAEA update published on or before 1 Oct (cadence is roughly weekly: 366 on 11 Sep, 367 on 17 Sep), which discounts a late-September restoration by a further ~20%. Evidence in the YES direction is limited to stated intent (plant management wanting to cut diesel dependence, onset of winter, active IAEA brokering) and the precedent that a comparable outage was resolved in ~30 days in late 2025 — but that blocker was line damage reachable under a ceasefire, not destroyed substation equipment. Thin, one-sided evidence on substation progress keeps me near the base rate.

EVENT WINDOW: 12 Sep 2026 -> 1 Oct 2026 (resolution stamp 2026-10-02T00:00Z) per the criteria; as of 2026-09-21T13:26Z, ~48% elapsed, ~10 days remain.

TIMELINE / EVIDENCE
- 24 Mar 2026: Dniprovska 750 kV line disconnected due to military activity (IAEA updates; background).
- Late May 2026: an electrical substation ~100 km northwest of ZNPP, on Ukrainian-controlled territory, damaged during military activity; IAEA experts who visited observed severe damage to essential equipment (World Nuclear News, 26 Jun 2026).
- 5 Jun 2026: IAEA brokers a localized ceasefire enabling demining and repair of the Dniprovska line itself (Al Jazeera, 5 Jun 2026; WNN).
- 21 Jun 2026: line repairs completed — cables replaced, a tower support arm replaced, new insulators installed (Rosatom/OSN; Ukrinform, 26 Jun 2026).
- 26 Jun 2026: IAEA states the line is repaired but cannot be returned to operation because of the substation damage; repair work on the substation is ongoing and 'completion is not expected in the near future' (Ukrainska Pravda; Ekonomichna Pravda; WNN).
- 20 Aug 2026: ZNPP loses Ferosplavna-1 (military activity north of the Dnipro), beginning its 26th loss of off-site power. Russian side states Kyiv has not supplied voltage to the repaired Dniprovska line (Prime/RIA, 20 Aug 2026).
- 5-7 Sep 2026: seventh IAEA-brokered localized ceasefire; demining and repair restore Ferosplavna-1 on the evening of 7 Sep, ending the 26th LOOP (IAEA; anews, 5 Sep 2026).
- 11 Sep 2026 (IAEA Update 366): 'the 750 kV Dniprovska line remains unavailable despite repairs completed in June under a previous IAEA-brokered ceasefire because of severe damage at the associated electrical substation.' Pre-war the site had 10 external lines; it now relies on the single 330 kV Ferosplavna-1.
- 17 Sep 2026 (IAEA Update 367): refers to 'the ZNPP's sole remaining external power line — the 330 kV Ferosplavna-1'; no mention of Dniprovska or the substation; notes serious risks remain and that additional diesel fuel delivery is needed. Drone counts reported at Rivne (8), South Ukraine (35), Chornobyl (48).
- 20 Sep 2026: ZNPP communications director Evgeniya Yashina (TASS/Ridus) states the plant seeks to commission the repaired Dniprovska line to cut dependence on diesel fuel and on the single remaining line; confirms it was repaired 21 Jun and remains not connected to the system.
- Attribution of the blocker differs by side: IAEA/Ukrainian reporting cites substation equipment damage; Russian/plant statements frame it as Ukraine not energising the line and not communicating a timetable (RIA, 26 Jun 2026). Both are consistent with the line being unenergised.
- Contrasting precedent from the prior year: after a 30-day total loss of off-site power in autumn 2025, the repaired Dniprovska line was energised by the Ukrainian grid operator and the 750 kV switchyard repowered two minutes later, with all diesel generators off within hours (WNN, 2025). That blocker was line damage repaired under a ceasefire zone, not substation equipment.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: the Dniprovska line is described by the IAEA as unavailable; absent a change it stays so and the last-known-status clause applies.

BASE RATES / COUNTS
- Over the 92 days from repair completion (21 Jun 2026) to 21 Sep 2026: zero reconnections of Dniprovska; approximately nine consecutive non-overlapping 10-day windows, none containing a reconnection.
- Over the full outage: 181 days unavailable since 24 Mar 2026.
- Conditional on the blocker being substation/switchyard equipment damage rather than line damage (the currently known condition): no instance in this conflict of such a blocker being cleared within a 10-day window; the one comparable 750 kV restoration (2025) was conditioned on line-only damage plus a ceasefire, and took ~30 days from outage start.
- ZNPP losses of off-site power: 26 to date in the conflict, of which reportedly 14-15 occurred in 2026 alone — i.e. the grid connection environment is highly volatile in the NO-preserving direction as well (Ferosplavna-1 losses do not affect this question).
- IAEA update cadence over the relevant period: 366 on 11 Sep, 367 on 17 Sep — roughly weekly, implying one or two further updates (approximately 24 Sep and approximately 1 Oct) fall inside the window; publication of an approximately-1-Oct update on or before 1 Oct is not guaranteed.

DECIDING-BODY / SOURCE CALENDAR: IAEA DG updates are numbered and published roughly weekly on iaea.org and mirrored on ReliefWeb and globalsecurity.org; IAEA Board of Governors met 7 Sep 2026 (DG introductory statement covers Ukraine). No published schedule for substation repair completion was found: searched, absent.

SEARCHED BUT NOT FOUND: any report after 26 Jun 2026 giving the substation's repair progress, procurement status, or an estimated completion date; any announcement of an eighth IAEA-brokered ceasefire or of one covering substation work; any Ukrenergo/Ministry of Energy statement on energising the Dniprovska line; any IAEA update numbered 368 or later; any prediction market (Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, bookmakers) on ZNPP power-line status — Polymarket carries only ZNPP 'explosion by date' markets.

calls.reasoning: Status quo is firmly NO and the resolution rule defaults to NO on silence. IAEA Update 366 (11 Sep 2026) states Dniprovska 'remains unavailable despite repairs completed in June ... because of severe damage at the associated electrical substation'; Update 367 (17 Sep) still calls Ferosplavna-1 the 'sole remaining external power line'; ZNPP's own communications director confirmed on 20 Sep the repaired line is not connected. The binding constraint is destroyed 750 kV substation equipment ~100 km NW on Ukrainian-controlled territory, which the IAEA/WNN described in late June as not expected to be completed in the near term, with zero published progress in the ~3 months since. Conditional base rate: 0 of ~9 consecutive 10-day windows since the substation became the blocker; 0 of ~18 since the 24 Mar disconnection. With ~10 days left, YES additionally requires the restoration to appear in an IAEA update published on or before 1 Oct (next due ~24 Sep and ~1 Oct), a further ~15-20% haircut. The one genuine YES-side asymmetry is that this blocker sits far behind Ukrainian lines and so needs no brokered ceasefire, meaning completion could arrive without the weeks of public signalling that preceded every past ZNPP line restoration -- but long-lead HV equipment plus three months of no reported progress outweighs the unobservability.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs shared the same factual spine and clustered at 0.04-0.05, so reconciliation was about weighing two judgment splits rather than settling contested facts. (1) Run 1's argument that the blocker sits in Ukrainian-held territory >100 km from the front and so needs no IAEA-brokered ceasefire -- making a completion potentially unsignalled, unlike every prior ZNPP restoration -- is valid and is why Run 1 sat a point higher; I weighed it against Runs 2/3's point that the June IAEA/WNN characterization ('not expected to be completed in the near term') was about the repair timeline itself, not its visibility, and that long-lead 750 kV equipment plus three months of silence dominates. I resolved toward the slower reading. (2) The reporting-lag discount (Run 3: ~20%; Runs 1/2: 'minor') is a judgment call worth well under a point on an already-thin YES path; I applied a ~15-20% haircut. (3) FACTUAL and unsettled: whether the binding constraint is destroyed substation equipment (IAEA/Ukrainian account) or simply Kyiv not energizing the line (Rosatom, 12 Sep). No web access on this run and no dossier source adjudicates it; I let it carry its uncertainty, noting both accounts are equally consistent with the line being unenergized today and neither signals imminent change. (4) The 2025 precedent of a ~30-day Dniprovska outage ending with near-instant energization is the strongest YES analogue but does not transfer: that blocker was line damage reachable under a ceasefire zone. I carried Run 2/3's conditional base rate (0 of ~9 ten-day windows under the current blocker) forward as the anchor. I retrieved nothing myself this run, so sources is empty. No prediction market exists on this event -- all three runs independently checked Polymarket, Manifold, and Kalshi and found none (Polymarket carries only ZNPP 'explosion by date' contracts), so there is no crowd anchor and none was blended.
